questions.question: In Kafka, what does a partition give you?
options: A separate database for each consumer
An ordered slice of a topic that can be read in parallel
A copy of the Spring Boot application
questions.explanation: A topic is split into partitions. Each keeps its events in order, and a consumer group reads different partitions in parallel.

questions.question: Which Spring Boot 4 starter adds Kafka support?
questions.explanation: spring-boot-starter-kafka brings Spring for Apache Kafka, with KafkaTemplate and @KafkaListener.

questions.question: Two listeners use groupId 'sms' and groupId 'email' on the same topic. One event is sent. How many times is a listener method called in total?
questions.explanation: Each consumer group receives its own copy of every event, so both listeners get it once.

questions.question: Events (key P101, 'Picked up') then (key P101, 'Out for delivery') are sent to a topic with 3 partitions. In what order does the consumer see the two P101 events?
options: Out for delivery, then Picked up
Picked up, then Out for delivery
Only the last one is delivered
questions.explanation: The same key goes to the same partition, and a partition keeps the order in which events were written.

questions.question: Two different services use the same consumer group id, and each was expected to receive every event. Instead, each sees only about half. What is the bug?
options: The topic has too many replicas
The events are missing a key
They share one group, so the partitions are split between them
questions.explanation: Consumers in one group share the work. Each service needs its own group id to get a full copy.
